import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 848

Is the maximum size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never
squarefree (for all $a, b \in A$) achieved by taking those $n \equiv 7 \pmod{25}$?

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
 - [Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics,
   and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade
   de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
 - [Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025)
   https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
 - Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
-/

namespace Erdos848

/-- A set $A$ has the non-squarefree product property if $ab + 1$ is not squarefree
for all $a, b ∈ A$. -/
def NonSquarefreeProductProp (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ¬Squarefree (a * b + 1)

/-- The candidate extremal set: $\{n ∈ \{0, \dots, N-1\} : n ≡ 7 (mod 25)\}$. -/
def A₇ (N : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range N).filter (fun n => n % 25 = 7)

/-- The Erdős Problem 848 statement for a fixed $N$: any set $A ⊆ \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ with
the non-squarefree product property has cardinality at most $|A₇(N)|$. -/
def Erdos848For (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.range N → NonSquarefreeProductProp A →
    A.card ≤ (A₇ N).card

/-- Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_848 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ N, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

/-- There exists $N₀$ such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfies that $ab + 1$
is never squarefree for all $a, b ∈ A$, then $|A| ≤ |\{n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}|$.

More precisely, Sawhney proves: there exist absolute constants $η > 0$ and $N₀$
such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $|A| ≥ (1/25 - η)N$ then $A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}$ or
$A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 18 \pmod{25}\}$.

A complete formal Lean 4 proof is available at:
https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger/blob/1cc2ac8e9d70516e979733c6ea5c4d2eb652d1f5/formal/lean/Erdos/848.lean"]
theorem erdos_848.variants.asymptotic : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

end Erdos848

findings.description: The module bibliography conflates two Erdős papers. The entry labelled [Er92b] gives the title, journal, year, and pages of [Er95], the 1995 Resenhas paper. The source of Problem 848 is instead Problem 23 on page 239 of the 1992 Le Matematiche paper. This is a reference error; the mathematical statements remain intact.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/848 cites [Er92b,p.239]. The entries https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er92b and https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er95 distinguish the two papers. In the original [Er92b], Problem 23, p.239, Erdős writes: “Assume next that a_i a_j + 1 is never squarefree. This is satisfied if a_i ≡ 7 (mod 25). Is this sequence maximal?” Original paper: https://lematematiche.dmi.unict.it/index.php/lematematiche/article/download/587/555.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er92b] bibliography entry with: Erdős, P., “Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics,” Le Matematiche (Catania) 47(2) (1992), 231–240, Problem 23, p.239.

status_issues.recorded: @[category research solved] and answer(True) for the all-N question.
status_issues.source_status: The source labels Problem 848 “DECIDABLE — Resolved up to a finite check.” Sawhney's 2025 result proves the bound only for sufficiently large N; the all-N question is not recorded as settled.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/848 explicitly displays “Resolved up to a finite check” and says the problem was solved “for all sufficiently large N.” Sawhney's Proposition 1.1 begins “There exists an integer N₀ such that if N ≥ N₀ then …”. The exact linked external Lean file likewise says “The full Erdős conjecture (∀ N) remains open” immediately above problem_848_asymptotic.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep the all-N proposition, which faithfully states the question, but change its category to research open and its answer to answer(sorry). Leave erdos_848.variants.asymptotic marked research solved.

reformulations.difference: The helpers use {0,…,N−1} rather than {1,…,N}, and maximality is expressed as a universal cardinality upper bound without explicitly asserting that the candidate attains it.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let P(N) denote the source's upper bound over Finset.Icc 1 N. An admissible A cannot contain 0, since its diagonal pair would require ¬Squarefree 1. Therefore P(N) ↔ Erdos848For (N+1), and the corresponding candidates are equal: SourceA7 N = A₇ (N+1). Erdos848For 0 also holds. Consequently both the universal and the eventually-atTop formulations are unchanged by this reindexing. Finally A₇ N is itself admissible: for any a,b in it, ab+1 ≡ 7·7+1 ≡ 0 modulo 25, so it is not squarefree. Hence the universal upper bound is equivalent to the candidate attaining the maximum. These equivalences and admissibility were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the sorry-backed problem theorems.

review.notes: No substantive mathematical misformalization was found among the three definitions and two theorem statements. Lean boundary tests and finite searches at selected N through 100 passed; an independent exact maximum-clique search found no counterexample for source intervals 0 ≤ N ≤ 500. The linked external theorem states precisely the eventual bound, and static inspection found no sorry holes or custom axioms. Its full proof certificate was not independently rechecked: the external project pins Lean/Mathlib v4.27.0, whereas the supplied sandbox uses v4.33.1 and encountered compatibility errors. Those errors are not treated as evidence against the formal_proof record. All review artifacts are under /workspace/review; the reviewed file was not modified.
